supportDesc.foliation: Modern foliation in pencil. Inserted leaves of smaller size numbered 63a, 65a, 66a, 148a and one without folation (62a).

collation.p: Parchment guards, some with visible text.
The collation is tentative. The volume probably consists of several separate codicological units (not recorded here).

p.note: Top of page, in brown ink by a contemporary hand: Carthusiensium prope erffordiam est hic liber et continetur in eo, followed by four lines of text: Contractus de diuersis exemplis ex diuersis historiis et libris et hic abbreuiata sunt super quo vide folio 14 in secunda columpna Quomodo et ex quibus compilator huiusmodi extraxit [...] followed by a table of contents. In brown ink by a modern hand: Inköpt till Kgl. Bibliotheket från G. Stephens 23/10 1848. Middle of page, in brown ink by a contemporary hand: Domini Iohannis Staubmels baccalareus theologie et monachus huius domus. In pencil by a modern hand: 242 Blätt. Lower right corner: National Library book label with current signum.

binding.p: Medieval binding. Brown leather over wooden boards. Three double raised bands. Hook and clasp fastenings remaining on and , the strap is lost. On , fragments of a parchment label with partly legible text, beginning Collaciones capitulares, and a second strip of paper with illegible text. On , remnants of a paper label and current signum stamped in gold.

decoNote.p: Tooled in blind in a geometrical pattern of double-lined lozenges.

binding.condition: The leather has been cut, exposing the wood on both and . Board attachments exposed on . The is loose. Holes caused by insects on and .

provenance.p:
Salvatorberg charterhouse, Erfurt. Following the closure of the charterhouse in , the library was dispersed, see Eifler (2018)
. In the medieval catalogue of Salvatorberg library, the manuscript had the signum O 105, see Lehmann (1928)
.

The volume appears in the sale catalogue of the book collector Friedrich Gottlieb Julius von Bülow (Bibliotheca Büloviana) as lot 437, see Schäffer (1836)
. The volume was purchased at the auction by George Stephens.

acquisition.p: Purchased by the Royal Library from George Stephens in .

summary.p: Compilation of sermons from Salvatorberg charterhouse, Erfurt.
